intent.raw_query: Amsterdam museums and canals, $2200 solo, 5 days, May 2027, from NYC

experiences.description: Explore the Netherlands' premier art and history museum, home to masterpieces by Rembrandt and Vermeer. The stunning building itself is a work of art, and the collection spans 800 years of Dutch history including the famous Night Watch painting.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Amsterdam
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

experiences.name: Jordaan Neighborhood Food & Canal Walk
experiences.description: Stroll through Amsterdam's most picturesque neighborhood, stopping at local stroopwafel bakeries, artisan cheese shops, and traditional Dutch brown cafes (bruine kroegen). End with a canal-side Dutch bitterballen snack platter and local craft beer at a waterfront terrace.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Amsterdam Airport Schiphol at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Take the direct train from Schiphol to Amsterdam Centraal (20 min, ~€5.40). Check in to Canal House Amsterdam and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Jordaan Neighborhood Food & Canal Walk: After settling in, explore the charming Jordaan district on foot. Stroll along the Prinsengracht and Brouwersgracht canals, browse local shops, and pick up a fresh stroopwafel from a street stall. This is a great low-cost way to orient yourself to the city and soak in the iconic canal atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Wander along the Herengracht (Golden Bend) at dusk for stunning canal house reflections. Grab a spot along a canal bridge to watch the evening light — completely free and quintessentially Amsterdam.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport). Grab a quick snack at Schiphol if needed (~€5–8).
meals.lunch: Pick up a broodje (Dutch sandwich) from a local bakery or Albert Heijn supermarket near the hotel (~€4–6).
meals.dinner: Vleminckx Sauzenwinkel or a nearby FEBO (Dutch fast-food automat) for budget-friendly Dutch snacks like frites met mayo (~€6–10). Alternatively, try Soup en Zo for hearty soup and bread (~€8).

day_by_day.notes: Since the flight lands at 13:00, allow roughly 1.5–2 hours for immigration, baggage, and the train ride before reaching the hotel. Don't over-schedule Day 1 — the Jordaan walk is relaxed and flexible. Buy an OV-chipkaart at Schiphol for easy public transit use throughout the trip (~€7.50 deposit + top-up).

day_by_day.morning: Rijksmuseum Visit: Open from 9:00. Arrive early to beat the crowds. Explore masterpieces by Rembrandt (The Night Watch) and Vermeer (The Milkmaid). Budget 2.5–3 hours. Admission is ~€22.50 per adult — book online in advance to save time and sometimes find slight discounts.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Rijksmuseum, walk through the adjacent Museumplein and relax by the iconic 'I Amsterdam' letters area (free). Then head to the nearby Vondelpark for a peaceful afternoon stroll — Amsterdam's most beloved green space and completely free. Bring a snack and enjoy the outdoor atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the De Pijp neighborhood (a short walk from Vondelpark). Browse the Albert Cuyp Market if still open (closes ~17:00 on Sundays, check seasonal hours) for cheap local snacks. Then enjoy the vibrant, multicultural street atmosphere of De Pijp in the evening.

meals.breakfast: Albert Heijn supermarket near the hotel — grab yogurt, fruit, and a coffee (~€4–6). Many canal house hotels offer basic breakfast; check if included.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the Rijksmuseum café (budget option: soup + roll ~€8–10) or pack a supermarket lunch to eat in Vondelpark (~€5).
meals.dinner: Warung Spang-Makandra in De Pijp — authentic Surinamese-Javanese food, incredibly affordable and filling (~€10–13). One of Amsterdam's best budget dining secrets.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Rijksmuseum online at rijksmuseum.nl well in advance — it frequently sells out, especially on weekends. The Museumplein area is walkable from the Canal House hotel in about 20–25 minutes or take tram 2 or 12.

day_by_day.morning: Anne Frank House Tour: Opens at 9:00. This is Amsterdam's most emotionally powerful experience — walk through the secret annex where Anne Frank and her family hid during WWII. Budget 1.5–2 hours. Admission ~€16 per adult. CRITICAL: Tickets must be booked online months in advance at annefrank.org — they almost never have walk-in availability.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Anne Frank House (located in the Jordaan), continue exploring the surrounding Jordaan neighborhood more deeply. Visit the Noordermarkt area, peek into the Westerkerk (free to enter the church), and browse the boutique shops along Haarlemmerdijk street. Cross the charming Brouwersgracht canal for great photo opportunities.
day_by_day.evening: Take a self-guided evening canal walk along the Nine Streets (De Negen Straatjes) — a grid of charming streets with vintage shops, cafés, and beautiful canal views. This area is especially lovely at dusk when the canal houses are lit up.

meals.breakfast: Café Winkel 43 near the Noordermarkt — famous for apple pie (~€4) and coffee (~€3). A beloved Amsterdam institution and very budget-friendly.
meals.lunch: Grab a herring (haring) from a street fish cart near the Anne Frank House — a classic Dutch experience for ~€4–5. Add a small cone of frites for ~€3.
meals.dinner: Moeders restaurant in the Jordaan — a quirky, homey Dutch restaurant with generous portions of traditional Dutch food. Mains ~€14–18. Slightly above bare budget but worth it for the authentic experience. Alternatively, cook in if the hotel has facilities, using Albert Heijn groceries (~€8–10).

day_by_day.notes: The Anne Frank House is a short 10-minute walk from Canal House Amsterdam. Bring tissues — the experience is deeply moving. Photography is not permitted inside the annex. Arrive a few minutes early for your time slot.

day_by_day.morning: Van Gogh Museum Experience: Opens at 9:00. Immerse yourself in the world's largest collection of Van Gogh's works, including Sunflowers, The Bedroom, and Almond Blossom. Budget 2–2.5 hours. Admission ~€22 per adult — book online at vangoghmuseum.nl in advance. Located on Museumplein, a short walk or tram ride from the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Van Gogh Museum, visit the free Stedelijk Museum garden area or simply walk along the Singelgracht canal back toward the city center. Stop by the Bloemenmarkt (Flower Market) on the Singel canal — the world's only floating flower market. Free to browse, and you can buy a small souvenir packet of tulip bulbs (~€5–8) to take home.
day_by_day.evening: Take a budget canal boat experience: instead of expensive guided tours (~€20+), look for the Canal Bus hop-on-hop-off day pass (~€26) or better yet, rent a small paddle boat or kayak for a 1-hour slot (~€12–15 per person) to explore the canals yourself at your own pace. Return to the hotel area for a relaxed evening.

meals.breakfast: Supermarket grab-and-go from Albert Heijn — coffee, a croissant, and fruit (~€4–5). Eat near Museumplein before the museum opens.
meals.lunch: Broodje Bert or any local sandwich shop near the Museumplein area (~€6–8 for a broodje and drink). Eat on a bench in the park to save money.
meals.dinner: Foodhallen Amsterdam (indoor food market in Oud-West, ~15 min by tram): a vibrant covered market with diverse food stalls. Budget ~€10–15 for a full meal from multiple vendors. Great atmosphere and variety.

day_by_day.notes: The Van Gogh Museum and Rijksmuseum are both on Museumplein — if you feel like a quick second look at the Rijksmuseum exterior or garden, it's right there. The Bloemenmarkt is a 20-minute walk north from Museumplein along the canals. Check paddle boat rental availability at Boaty or similar services near the Jordaan.

day_by_day.morning: Free Canal District Walking Tour: Spend your final morning doing a self-guided walk through Amsterdam's UNESCO-listed canal ring. Start at the Amstel River, walk along the Herengracht, Keizersgracht, and Prinsengracht. Visit the Magere Brug (Skinny Bridge) — a beautiful white drawbridge over the Amstel, free and iconic. Stop at the Begijnhof, a hidden medieval courtyard in the city center (free entry, opens ~9:00).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Amsterdam Museum (Amsterdams Historisch Museum) or explore the free FOAM Photography Museum lobby area. Alternatively, browse the Waterlooplein Flea Market (open Mon–Sat, free entry) for vintage finds and souvenirs at bargain prices. Do any last-minute souvenir shopping — Dutch stroopwafels from Albert Heijn are the best budget souvenir (~€3–5 per pack).
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in the Jordaan, then a last sunset canal walk. Head to the Westertoren (Westerkerk tower area) around golden hour for beautiful light on the canals. Pack bags and prepare for departure.

meals.breakfast: Treat yourself to a proper Dutch breakfast at Café de Jaren on the Amstel — eggs, bread, juice, and coffee for ~€10–12. A slightly splurge-worthy farewell breakfast with beautiful riverside views.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick kroket or broodje from FEBO (Dutch automat fast food) — a fun, cheap, and very Dutch experience (~€4–6).
meals.dinner: Festina Lente in the Jordaan — a cozy, unpretentious brown café (bruine kroeg) with affordable Dutch and European dishes (~€12–16 for mains). Great atmosphere for a final Amsterdam evening.

day_by_day.notes: Check your departure flight time and plan accordingly — if flying out on May 19, adjust the afternoon/evening schedule. Schiphol train from Amsterdam Centraal takes ~20 minutes; allow at least 2.5–3 hours before flight departure for check-out, travel, and airport security. Return or top up your OV-chipkaart balance at any station machine before leaving.

trip_options.title: Classic Amsterdam Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Amsterdam Airport Schiphol at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Take the direct train from Schiphol to Amsterdam Centraal (±17 min), then taxi or tram to Canal House Amsterdam. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Jordaan Neighborhood Food & Canal Walk: After settling in, take a leisurely stroll through the iconic Jordaan district. Pick up a fresh stroopwafel from a local bakery, browse artisan shops, and soak in the atmosphere of the historic canal-side streets. This is an ideal gentle introduction to Amsterdam without heavy scheduling after a flight.
day_by_day.evening: Wander along the Prinsengracht and Keizersgracht canals at dusk — the bridges and canal houses are beautifully lit in the evening. Enjoy a relaxed dinner near the Jordaan area and unwind after your travel day.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a light snack at Schiphol Airport before landing.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite near Amsterdam Centraal or at the hotel — try Broodje Bert or a nearby Dutch sandwich shop for a classic broodje kroket (€5–10).
meals.dinner: Café de Reiger (Jordaan) — a beloved neighbourhood bistro with Dutch-French cuisine. Expect mains around €18–26. Reservation recommended.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Focus on getting comfortable with the neighbourhood and the canal layout. Canal House Amsterdam is ideally located for walking to most Jordaan highlights.

day_by_day.morning: Rijksmuseum Visit: Spend the morning at the Netherlands' premier art and history museum. Arrive at opening (9:00) to beat crowds. Highlights include Rembrandt's 'The Night Watch,' Vermeer's 'The Milkmaid,' and the stunning Great Hall. Plan 2.5–3 hours. Book tickets online in advance (€22.50/person).
day_by_day.afternoon: Private Canal Boat Tour: After the Rijksmuseum, head to a nearby canal dock and board a private or small-group canal boat tour of Amsterdam's UNESCO-listed canal ring. Glide past 17th-century merchant houses, hidden gardens, and iconic bridges. Tours typically last 1–1.5 hours. A perfect way to see the city from the water.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Leidseplein area — Amsterdam's lively entertainment square. Browse street performers, enjoy a pre-dinner drink at a canal-side terrace bar, then head to dinner nearby.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or visit Café Winkel 43 in the Jordaan for their famous apple pie and coffee (€8–12).
meals.lunch: Grab a quick lunch near Museumplein — try Loetje aan de Gracht for a classic Dutch beef sandwich or burger (€12–16).
meals.dinner: Restaurant Blauw (Amstelveenseweg area) — excellent Indonesian rijsttafel (rice table), a Dutch colonial tradition. Budget €25–35 per person. Reservation strongly recommended.

day_by_day.notes: Sunday mornings at the Rijksmuseum can be busy — arriving right at 9:00 is key. The canal boat tour is best booked in advance; many depart from near the Rijksmuseum or Leidsegracht. Wear comfortable shoes for the afternoon walk.

day_by_day.morning: Anne Frank House Tour: One of Amsterdam's most moving and important experiences. Walk through the hidden annex where Anne Frank and her family hid during WWII. Tickets MUST be booked weeks in advance online (€16/person) — same-day entry is virtually impossible. Allow 1.5–2 hours. Located on Prinsengracht, a short walk from the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Van Gogh Museum Experience: Head to the Van Gogh Museum on Museumplein (a short tram ride from the Anne Frank House). Immerse yourself in the world's largest collection of Van Gogh's works, including 'Sunflowers' and 'The Bedroom.' Book tickets online in advance (€22/person). Allow 1.5–2 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the canal area for a relaxed evening. Consider renting a pedal boat or kayak on the canals for a fun DIY water experience at golden hour. Then enjoy dinner in the De Pijp neighbourhood, Amsterdam's vibrant multicultural district.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or visit Scandinavian Embassy café for excellent specialty coffee and open-faced sandwiches (€10–15).
meals.lunch: Grab a light lunch between museums at Museumplein — try Foodhallen (indoor food market) in the Oud-West for diverse, affordable options (€10–15).
meals.dinner: Brouwerij 't IJ or dinner at Bar Fisk in De Pijp — great for fresh North Sea fish dishes and Dutch craft beer. Mains €16–24.

day_by_day.notes: This is your most culturally intensive day — pace yourself. The Anne Frank House is emotionally heavy; give yourself quiet reflection time afterward. Both museums are best visited on weekdays to avoid peak weekend crowds. Confirm your Anne Frank House booking well before the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Zaanse Schans: Take a short train + bus journey (~40 min from Amsterdam Centraal) to this open-air museum village featuring authentic working windmills, wooden houses, a clog-maker, and a cheese farm. A quintessential Dutch experience away from the city bustle. Free entry to the village; individual attractions €4–8 each.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Amsterdam by early afternoon and explore the Eastern Docklands (NDSM or Java Island area) — a fascinating post-industrial neighbourhood with striking modern architecture, street art, and canal views. Alternatively, visit the Hermitage Amsterdam area or browse the Waterlooplein flea market for unique souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Amsterdam's vibrant Nieuwmarkt square for evening drinks at a traditional Dutch 'bruine kroeg' (brown café). Enjoy the lively atmosphere and end the evening with a canal-side stroll back to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel or grab a croissant and coffee at a bakery near Amsterdam Centraal before the train.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Zaanse Schans — try the on-site pancake restaurant for traditional Dutch poffertjes or pannenkoeken (€12–18).
meals.dinner: In de Waag restaurant at Nieuwmarkt — a stunning 15th-century gatehouse converted into a candlelit restaurant. Dutch-European cuisine, mains €20–28. Atmospheric and memorable.

day_by_day.notes: Leave for Zaanse Schans by 9:00–9:30 to make the most of the morning before crowds arrive. The village is free to enter but bring cash for individual attractions. Comfortable walking shoes are essential. Check train schedules from Amsterdam Centraal to Koog-Zaandijk station.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning — revisit your favourite canal neighbourhood or explore the Nine Streets (De Negen Straatjes), a charming grid of specialty boutiques, vintage shops, and artisan cafés connecting the main canals. Perfect for last-minute gift shopping and relaxed browsing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Amsterdam Museum or the Foam Photography Museum (Keizersgracht) for a lighter cultural experience. Foam is particularly excellent for contemporary photography and is set in a beautiful canal house (€15/person). Afterward, take one final slow walk along the Herengracht — Amsterdam's most elegant canal — and stop at a terrace café for a farewell coffee or Dutch beer.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in the city centre, then pack and prepare for departure. Depending on your return flight time, you may have time for a final evening canal stroll or drinks at a rooftop bar like SkyLounge Amsterdam (Doubletree Hotel) for panoramic city views.

meals.breakfast: Treat yourself to a full Dutch breakfast at Café Papeneiland — one of Amsterdam's oldest brown cafés, dating to 1642, on Prinsengracht (€10–15).
meals.lunch: Light lunch at one of the Nine Streets cafés — try Greenwoods for English-style sandwiches and soups (€12–16).
meals.dinner: Rijsel (Marcusstraat) — a beloved Amsterdam restaurant in a converted school gymnasium, serving French-Flemish rotisserie chicken and seasonal dishes. Excellent value, mains €18–26. Book ahead.

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if your flight is in the evening. Amsterdam Centraal to Schiphol Airport takes ~17 minutes by direct train (4–6 trains per hour). Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security. OV-chipkaart (public transport card) is the easiest way to travel around the city all week.

day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Canal House Amsterdam and settle into your suite. Take a leisurely self-guided stroll along the Herengracht and Keizersgracht canals directly from the hotel to orient yourself with the neighborhood. Stop at a local pâtisserie for a coffee and stroopwafel.
day_by_day.evening: Private Canal Boat Tour — board a beautifully appointed private canal boat at sunset for a 2-hour cruise through Amsterdam's UNESCO-listed canal ring. Glide past 17th-century merchant houses, arched bridges, and illuminated waterways as the city lights come alive.

meals.breakfast: Enjoyed on the flight or at the airport upon arrival — no hotel breakfast on Day 1.
meals.lunch: Light bite near the hotel after check-in: Café Papeneiland, a historic brown café on the Prinsengracht serving traditional Dutch open-faced sandwiches and soups.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ciel Bleu (Hotel Okura) — two Michelin-starred restaurant offering exquisite contemporary French-Dutch cuisine with panoramic Amsterdam skyline views. Reserve in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer before arrival. Book the Private Canal Boat Tour for sunset departure (approximately 19:30 in May). Confirm Ciel Bleu reservation well in advance as tables are limited.

day_by_day.morning: Rijksmuseum Visit — spend a rich morning at the Netherlands' premier art and history museum. Admire masterpieces by Rembrandt, Vermeer, and Frans Hals. Opt for a private guided tour (bookable through the hotel concierge) to bypass queues and gain deeper insight into the Golden Age collection. Allow 2.5–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Van Gogh Museum Experience — just steps from the Rijksmuseum, immerse yourself in the world's largest collection of Van Gogh's works including Sunflowers and The Bedroom. Pre-book timed entry tickets. Afterward, relax in the elegant Museumplein gardens with a glass of champagne from a nearby terrace café.
day_by_day.evening: Jordaan Neighborhood Food & Canal Walk — as the afternoon light softens, explore Amsterdam's most picturesque neighborhood. Visit artisan cheese shops, a stroopwafel bakery, and browse the antique galleries along the Bloemgracht canal.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast at Canal House Amsterdam — enjoy a curated spread of fresh pastries, Dutch cheeses, smoked salmon, and seasonal fruit in the elegant dining room.
meals.lunch: Librije's Zusje Amsterdam (Waldorf Astoria) — a Michelin-starred lunch experience offering refined Dutch cuisine in a stunning canal-house setting. Alternatively, a lighter option at Café Loetje for premium Dutch beef burgers.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurant Vinkeles (Dylan Hotel) — housed in an 18th-century former bakery, this Michelin-starred gem offers an intimate tasting menu with exceptional Dutch produce and an outstanding wine list.

day_by_day.notes: Book private guided Rijksmuseum tour and Van Gogh Museum timed-entry tickets at least 2 weeks in advance, especially for a Saturday. The Museumplein area can be busy — arrive at the Rijksmuseum by 09:30 to enjoy a quieter experience.

day_by_day.morning: Anne Frank House Tour — a profoundly moving and essential Amsterdam experience. Walk through the hidden annex where Anne Frank and her family hid during World War II. Book the earliest available timed-entry slot (08:00 or 09:00) for the most reflective, crowd-free experience. Allow 1.5–2 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private Canal Boat Tour (second experience, different route) — embark on a bespoke private boat tour focusing on the lesser-known eastern canal ring and the Amstel River. Your private captain will share stories of Amsterdam's merchant history. Enjoy chilled champagne and Dutch bitterballen on board.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Nine Streets (De Negen Straatjes) — a charming grid of boutique-lined streets between the main canals. Browse luxury Dutch design shops, independent perfumeries, and high-end vintage fashion before heading to dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Dignita Hoftuin — a beautifully designed café in a historic courtyard garden near the Jordaan, offering organic, seasonal breakfast bowls, avocado toast, and specialty coffee.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style luxury lunch on the private canal boat — arranged by the hotel concierge with a hamper from Marqt organic market including artisan cheeses, charcuterie, fresh bread, and local craft beer or rosé.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Breda — a celebrated Amsterdam restaurant with a creative, produce-driven menu and a relaxed yet sophisticated atmosphere. Excellent natural wine selection.

day_by_day.notes: Anne Frank House tickets must be booked online months in advance — this is non-negotiable. Sunday morning is ideal for a quieter visit. Coordinate the afternoon boat tour pick-up point near the Westerkerk for seamless logistics.

day_by_day.morning: Stedelijk Museum — visit Amsterdam's world-class museum of modern and contemporary art and design, located steps from the Rijksmuseum. Explore works by Mondrian, Malevich, and Warhol alongside cutting-edge Dutch design. A quieter, more contemplative museum experience ideal for Monday mornings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private Walking Tour of the Canal Ring — arrange a private architectural historian guide through the hotel concierge for a 2.5-hour deep-dive into Amsterdam's UNESCO World Heritage canal ring. Discover hidden courtyards (hofjes), the history of the Dutch Golden Age merchant houses, and secret garden entrances not visible to regular tourists.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at Moon Amsterdam — the rotating rooftop restaurant and bar atop the A'DAM Tower offers spectacular 360-degree panoramic views of Amsterdam. Enjoy cocktails as the city glows in the evening light before descending for dinner.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast at Canal House Amsterdam — take your time with a full Dutch spread including fresh herring, Gouda, warm pastries, and freshly squeezed juice.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Rijsel — a beloved Amsterdam institution serving exceptional rotisserie chicken and seasonal Flemish-inspired dishes in a converted school gymnasium. Relaxed, premium quality.
meals.dinner: Dinner at &samhoud;places — an innovative, avant-garde tasting menu restaurant offering a multi-sensory dining journey. One of Amsterdam's most unique fine-dining experiences with theatrical presentation.

day_by_day.notes: Book Moon Amsterdam for sunset cocktails (around 20:00 in May) and reserve your &samhoud;places dinner well in advance. The private canal walking tour can be arranged through the hotel concierge or via Context Travel for expert guides.

day_by_day.morning: Hermitage aan de Amstel / Foam Photography Museum — visit Foam, Amsterdam's celebrated photography museum on the Keizersgracht, for a final cultural morning. The intimate canal-house setting and world-class rotating exhibitions make it a hidden gem. Afterward, take a final slow walk along the Reguliersgracht, one of Amsterdam's most photogenic canal intersections.
day_by_day.afternoon: Luxury Shopping & Leisure — spend your final afternoon browsing the upscale boutiques of P.C. Hooftstraat (Amsterdam's premier luxury shopping street) for Dutch designers, international fashion houses, and fine jewelry. Return to Canal House Amsterdam for a spa treatment or in-room relaxation before departure preparations.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at Spectrum (Hotel W Amsterdam) — a Michelin-starred restaurant offering a spectacular tasting menu that celebrates the full diversity of Dutch regional cuisine and ingredients. A fitting and memorable conclusion to a premium Amsterdam journey.

meals.breakfast: Special farewell breakfast at Brasserie Ambassade (Ambassade Hotel) — an elegant canal-side breakfast with views over the Herengracht, featuring smoked salmon, Dutch pastries, and fine cheeses.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Toscanini — Amsterdam's finest Italian restaurant, beloved by locals and visitors alike, serving handmade pasta and seasonal Italian cuisine in a warm, convivial setting in the Jordaan.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Spectrum (Hotel W Amsterdam) — Michelin-starred tasting menu showcasing innovative Dutch cuisine with a theatrical, elegant presentation. Pair with the sommelier's wine flight for a complete luxury experience.

day_by_day.notes: If departing early on Day 6, arrange a private chauffeur transfer to Schiphol the night before. Confirm checkout time with Canal House Amsterdam. Spectrum dinner reservation should be made at least 3–4 weeks in advance. Consider purchasing a small gift from a Jordaan artisan shop or Dutch design store as a souvenir of the trip.

query: Amsterdam museums and canals, $2200 solo, 5 days, May 2027, from NYC
